features.title: Features
features.description: What LocalGateKeys does on Windows, in the browser, on iPhone and on Apple Watch: encrypted vault, fill and passkeys, two-factor codes, secure sharing, imports, backups and device sync.
features.everything-it-does-and.1: Everything it does, and where it does it
features.everything-it-does-and.2: All of this runs on your own devices: the Windows app, the browser extension and the iPhone app. Free holds up to 7 items; Pro removes the limit and adds sync, two-factor codes and documents.
features.everything-it-does-and.3: The LocalGateKeys Home page: password health, upcoming reminders, a one-time codes card with live two-factor codes, and a list of logins with site logos.
features.everything-it-does-and.4: Home: password health, reminders, live two-factor codes and your items. Demo vault with made-up accounts.
features.the-vault.3: Everything you save is encrypted with a key protected by your master password, using Argon2id and AES-256-GCM. Names, usernames and websites are encrypted too, not just passwords.
features.the-vault.5: Website and desktop app logins, passkeys, payment cards, bank accounts, identities, secure notes, documents, SSH keys, API keys, Wi-Fi networks, bookmarks, software licences, subscriptions, warranties and purchases, each with its own fields.
features.the-vault.7: Keep files such as scanned documents in the vault, up to 25 MB each. Each file is encrypted with its own key. Preview a document, save a copy or open it in another app. With sync, files travel to your other devices, still encrypted.
features.the-vault.9: Store a site's setup key and LocalGateKeys shows the current code at the top of the login, and on a One-time codes card on the Home page. Codes follow the TOTP standard (RFC 6238): 6 to 8 digits, 15 to 120 seconds, SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512.
features.v2.watch.title: Codes on Apple Watch (Pro)
features.v2.watch.body: Show the two-factor codes you choose on your Apple Watch, up to 10. The watch shows codes only, never passwords, and they keep working without the iPhone nearby.
features.the-vault.11: Choose Scan QR code and paste a snip of the site's two-factor QR code (Win+Shift+S), drop in an image, or hold it up to your webcam. Google Authenticator export QR codes work too. The image is read on your PC and never saved.
features.the-vault.13: Random passwords of 8 to 256 characters, or passphrases of 3 to 16 words.
features.the-vault.15: See which saved passwords are weak, reused, more than a year old or missing a two-factor code. Breach checks against Have I Been Pwned are off until you turn them on, run only when you start them, and send only five characters of a hash, never the password.
features.the-vault.17: Each item shows the site's icon, a built-in logo for well-known sites, or an icon for its kind, so you can spot it at a glance.
features.the-vault.19: Find items with a command palette (Ctrl+K), filter chips, favourites and your own collections. Sort the list by title, date modified or date created, with favourites first. Arrow keys, Enter and Ctrl+C work in the list straight from the search box.
features.the-vault.21: Deleted items go to the trash, and the message that confirms it has an Undo button. The trash empties itself after 30 days, or keeps everything until you empty it.
features.the-vault.23: When a login's password changes, up to 10 earlier passwords are kept for a year in its encrypted history. Copy one, or restore it.
features.the-vault.24: A GitHub login open in LocalGateKeys, with its current two-factor code at the top, then username, hidden password, website, notes and recovery codes.
features.the-vault.25: The current two-factor code sits at the top of the login.
features.the-vault.26: The password generator with a random 20-character password and options for length, letters, digits and symbols.
features.the-vault.27: The generator makes random passwords or passphrases.
features.the-vault.28: The Security center showing a score of 77 out of 100, with weak, reused, no two-factor and old passwords to review, and unlock and backup checks.
features.the-vault.29: The Security center lists what to fix first.
features.moving-in-and-out.3: Bring in exports from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass and KeePassXC (including .kdbx files), Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox and Safari, or any other CSV file. You review every item before anything is written, and the import never goes online. On iPhone, bring logins, two-factor codes and passkeys straight over from Apple Passwords (iOS 26 and later), or import a file from many password managers and authenticator apps.
features.moving-in-and-out.5: Export to an encrypted KeePass KDBX 4 file, or to Bitwarden-compatible CSV or JSON, or KeePass XML. Every export asks for your master password first.
features.v2.share.title: Share one item securely
features.v2.share.body: Send a login or note as a .lgkshare file or a QR code, locked with a six-word code that you tell the other person another way. It opens once, and three wrong codes destroy it. Passkeys, documents and items with an attached file cannot be shared.
features.filling-sign-ins.3: Fill and save logins on websites, including sign-ins that ask for the username and password on separate pages. The extension asks the app on your PC for logins that match the exact site, through a local helper. It also fills two-factor codes, addresses and payment cards.
features.filling-sign-ins.5: After you sign in, the extension offers to save a new login or update a changed password. You can turn the prompt off for any site from the toolbar button.
features.filling-sign-ins.7: Nothing is filled until you pick an account. Forms are not submitted for you unless you turn on "Sign in after filling" in Settings, and then only after a fill you started.
features.filling-sign-ins.9: When a website in Chrome or Edge offers a passkey, LocalGateKeys can save it in your vault and sign you in with it. You approve every passkey in the desktop app, with Windows Hello or your master password, and the browser's own passkey dialog is always one click away. The private key never leaves the app.
features.filling-sign-ins.11: Fill sign-in windows of Windows programs with a fill button beside the password field or a hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+Space). Each app is bound once, and fill is refused if the program, its window or its fields have changed since.
features.filling-sign-ins.13: Search your vault and copy from anywhere with a hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+K by default). Ctrl+Alt+L locks the vault at once.
features.filling-sign-ins.15: LocalGateKeys installs no keyboard hook, reads no screen content to find passwords, and injects nothing into other programs. If an app does not expose proper sign-in fields, it is not filled.
features.filling-sign-ins.16: A sign-in page with the LocalGateKeys browser extension offering two saved accounts for that site.
features.filling-sign-ins.17: The extension offers only the logins saved for the site you are on.
features.unlocking.3: At least 12 characters, never written to disk. It is the one thing that opens your vault, and we cannot reset it.
features.unlocking.5: Unlock with your fingerprint, face or PIN through Windows Hello, after you set it up in LocalGateKeys.
features.unlocking.7: An optional webcam face check for PCs without Windows Hello. It is a convenience, not certified anti-spoofing; prefer Windows Hello when you can.
features.unlocking.9: An optional 24-word phrase that can open the vault if you forget the master password. It is shown once and never stored by the app.
features.unlocking.11: The vault locks after a period you choose, and copied passwords are cleared from the clipboard. Only what LocalGateKeys copied is cleared.
features.backups.3: Daily or weekly, at a time you set. Each backup is a full encrypted file, checked after writing, with attachments included.
features.backups.4: Extra copy in a folder you choose
features.backups.5: Have each backup copied to a OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox or Proton Drive folder, or anywhere else. Only encrypted backup files are copied, never the live vault.
features.backups.7: Move selected items to another vault in an encrypted file protected by its own password.
features.backups.9: The iPhone and Android apps save an encrypted .lgkm backup with a password you choose. Restore it on any iPhone, Android phone, Mac or PC: it merges like sync and never wipes your vault.
features.sync-between-your-devices.3: Pair a PC or an iPhone once with a one-use QR code (between PCs you paste its text). When both are unlocked on the same network, they exchange changes directly over an authenticated, encrypted connection. Nothing goes through the internet. If a PC's address changes, Find again reconnects, and each device shows when it last synced.
features.sync-between-your-devices.5: If your devices are rarely on the same network, sync through a cloud folder you already use, such as Dropbox or iCloud Drive, protected by a sync password. The provider only ever stores encrypted files. You can use both routes.
features.sync-between-your-devices.7: Logins, notes, cards and your other items, and attached documents with their files. Collections stay on each device. Edits made on two devices at once keep both versions, and a delete moves the item to the trash on the others. If a device brings back an older copy of the vault, the Windows app warns you instead of accepting it.
features.sync-between-your-devices.9: The iPhone app syncs with your Windows PC and Mac. A free PC paired with an iPhone that has Pro takes the licence over sync and becomes Pro. Get it on the App Store.An iPhone app is coming. It will sync with your Windows PC. It is not available yet.
features.privacy.3: You never sign up or sign in. A Pro licence is a key you keep, checked on your device. On iPhone, Pro is an App Store purchase, and the app sends only the App Store receipt to our licence server.
features.privacy.5: The apps send no usage data, crash reports or analytics.
features.privacy.7: On by default. It blocks background internet requests and breach checks, and an update check asks you first.
features.privacy.9: To show a site's icon, the app downloads it from that site. This tells the site you have an account there, and nothing else. It is off by default: turn on "Show website icons" in Settings (strict offline mode must be off).
features.privacy.11: Checking for updates downloads one small signed file. The app never downloads or installs anything by itself.
features.v2.iphone.title: On iPhone
features.v2.iphone.autofill.title: AutoFill in Safari and apps
features.v2.iphone.autofill.body: Fill logins in Safari and other apps, with suggestions in the QuickType bar, and use LocalGateKeys for passkeys. On iOS 18 and later it also fills cards, addresses and other details in any text field. The Safari extension offers to save a new login after you sign in.
features.v2.iphone.unlock.title: Face ID, Touch ID or an app password
features.v2.iphone.unlock.body: The vault opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode, with no password to create. If others know your passcode, add an optional app password, backed by a 24-word recovery phrase.
features.v2.iphone.security.title: Security check
features.v2.iphone.security.body: The Security tab gives your vault a score and lists weak, reused and old passwords, and logins that could use two-factor codes. Breach checks stay off until you turn them on.
features.v2.iphone.safety.title: Recently deleted, history and reminders
features.v2.iphone.safety.body: Deleted items wait 30 days in Recently deleted, and Undo brings one straight back. Every login keeps its password history, and you can get a reminder before a card, passport or licence expires.
features.v2.iphone.files.title: Attached files (Pro)
features.v2.iphone.files.body: Attach documents and photos to your vault, stored encrypted and synced with your other devices.
features.v2.iphone.languages.title: Ten languages
features.v2.iphone.languages.body: The iPhone app speaks English, German, Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Dutch, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese and Simplified Chinese.
get_started.title: Get started
get_started.description: How to install LocalGateKeys on Windows, set up your vault, add the browser extension, and connect the iPhone, Apple Watch and Mac apps.
get_started.get-started.2: Install the Windows app, create your vault, then add the browser extension. It takes about five minutes, and you never need an account. Add the iPhone app whenever you like.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.2: LocalGateKeys runs on Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) and Windows 11, 64-bit, and comes from the Microsoft Store:
get_started.1-install-the-windows.3: Microsoft Store. The Store installs it and keeps it up to date. Open LocalGateKeys in the Microsoft Store, choose Get, then Open.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.4: Used the old installer? Uninstall it in Windows Settings › Apps (Installed apps on Windows 11, Apps & features on Windows 10), then install from the Microsoft Store. Your vault stays where it is, and the Store app opens it with the same master password.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.6: Get it from the Microsoft Store
get_started.2-create-your-vault.2: Open LocalGateKeys. On first start it asks you to create a vault, then a short setup guide offers Windows Hello, import, a recovery phrase and the browser extension. Skip any step and finish it later from the Finish setting up card.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.3: Choose a master password of at least 12 characters. Write it down and keep it somewhere safe. We never have it, so nobody can reset it for you.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.4: Open Security center in the sidebar and set up a recovery phrase. Keep it offline, for example on paper. It opens the vault if you forget the master password.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.5: In the same place, turn on Windows Hello if your PC has a fingerprint reader, a Hello camera or a PIN, so day-to-day unlocking is quick.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.6: Turn on scheduled backups in Settings and choose where the encrypted backup files go, such as a USB drive or a folder you already back up.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.7: The Security center with the password health score, items to fix, and the unlock and backup settings: master password, Windows Hello, recovery phrase, auto-lock and backups.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.8: The Security center keeps unlock methods, the recovery phrase and backups in one place.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.2: The extension fills sign-ins in your browser. It talks only to the LocalGateKeys app on the same PC, so install the app first.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.4: Microsoft Edge: open it in Edge Add-ons and choose Get.coming soon.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.5: Google Chrome: open it in the Chrome Web Store and choose Add to Chrome.coming soon to the Chrome Web Store.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.6: Pin it: open the browser's extensions menu (the puzzle-piece icon) and pin LocalGateKeys to the toolbar.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.7: Keep the app running and unlocked. Go to a sign-in page you have a login saved for: the extension offers only the logins saved for that exact site. Nothing fills until you click.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.8: Sign in somewhere new and the extension offers to save the login.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.9: Extension says it cannot reach the app? In the app, open Devices & connections and choose Repair bridge, then restart the browser.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.10: A sign-in page with the LocalGateKeys browser extension offering two saved accounts for that site.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.11: The extension offers only the logins saved for the site you are on.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.12: Mozilla Firefox (Windows): open it in Firefox Add-ons and choose Add to Firefox.
get_started.4-bring-your-passwords.2: Choose Import & export in the sidebar and pick an export file from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass or KeePassXC, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox or Safari, or any CSV. You review every item before anything is saved, and nothing goes online. Delete the export file afterwards, because most exports hold passwords in plain text.
get_started.4-bring-your-passwords.3: The free edition holds up to 7 items. Pro removes the limit.
get_started.5-fill-windows-apps.2: For programs such as game launchers, open a desktop login in the app and choose App binding… to bind it to the program's sign-in window once. After that, a fill button appears beside the password field, or you can press Ctrl+Shift+Space. LocalGateKeys refuses to fill if the program or window has changed since you bound it.
get_started.6-turn-on-pro.2: Pro is a single payment that adds unlimited items, sync between your devices, two-factor codes and documents. After you buy it, choose Install in LocalGateKeys on your licence page, or paste your licence key in Settings › Plan & sync › Licence. See your Pro licence.
get_started.v2.iphone.title: 7 Add your iPhone
get_started.v2.iphone.intro: The iPhone app keeps its own encrypted vault and syncs with your PC. Sync is part of Pro.
get_started.v2.iphone.1: Install LocalGateKeys from the App Store and open it.The iPhone app is not available yet.
get_started.v2.iphone.2: Tap Unlock. The vault opens with Face ID, Touch ID or your iPhone passcode, so there is no password to create. A short setup offers import, an optional app password and AutoFill.
get_started.v2.iphone.3: Turn on AutoFill: in LocalGateKeys choose Settings › AutoFill › Open AutoFill settings, then turn on LocalGateKeys under General › AutoFill & Passwords.
get_started.v2.iphone.4: Pair it with your PC: on the PC open Sync & devices, turn on Wi-Fi sync and choose Show QR code. On the iPhone open the Sync tab and tap Scan QR code. Check that both screens show the same code, then choose Accept on the PC.
get_started.v2.iphone.5: Apple Watch (Pro): install LocalGateKeys from the iPhone's Watch app, then open a login with a two-factor code and tap Show on Apple Watch.
get_started.v2.iphone.note: Bought Pro on the iPhone? Once paired, a free PC takes the licence over sync and becomes Pro. Help for every iPhone screen is in the user guide.
get_started.iphone-and-android.3: Mac and Android: both apps are coming. They are not available yet.
get_started.iphone-and-android.5: Stuck? See Support and FAQ or email {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}.

help.intro.5: Good to know on every device
help.intro.6: Your vault stays on your devices. There is no account and no LocalGateKeys server holding your passwords.
help.intro.7: Nobody can reset your master password or app password. Set up a recovery phrase and keep it on paper.
help.intro.8: Free holds up to 7 items. Pro ({{PRICE}}, paid once) adds unlimited items, two-factor codes, files and sync. Editing, deleting and filling items you already have are never blocked.
help.windows.3: Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) and Windows 11, 64-bit. Install it from the Microsoft Store or the download page.
help.windows.24: Open LocalGateKeys. Enter a Master password of at least 12 characters, type it again in Confirm password, and choose Create vault.
help.windows.25: The Set up LocalGateKeys guide follows, in five steps: create the vault, Set up Windows Hello, Import your passwords, Open recovery phrase (you retype three of its words to prove you saved it), and Test connection for the browser extension.
help.windows.26: You can Skip any step. Skipped steps wait on a Finish setting up card in the vault, with Continue setup and Hide.
help.windows.27: Tip. To see the guide again: Settings › Help & diagnostics › Show setup again.
help.windows.29: Each profile is a separate vault with its own master password, for example one for work and one for home.
help.windows.30: On the unlock screen choose Use another profile, then Create profile and type a Profile name.
help.windows.31: To edit a profile, press Ctrl+K and run Switch profile. There you can Add profile, Edit, set a Photo… and Accent colour, or Remove it.
help.windows.32: The tray menu's Lock & switch person locks and goes straight to the profile chooser.
help.windows.35: Unlock with Windows Hello: fingerprint, face or PIN. Set it up in Settings › Unlocking › Windows Hello › Set up. Start Windows Hello automatically (on by default) shows the prompt as soon as the window opens.
help.windows.36: Use camera instead: face matching with an ordinary webcam, done on the PC. It is less secure than Windows Hello. Set it up with Set up camera verification.
help.windows.38: On the unlock screen choose Forgot it? Use recovery phrase.
help.windows.39: Type the 24 words, separated by spaces.
help.windows.40: Choose a new master password (12 characters or more), type it twice and choose Recover vault.
help.windows.41: Afterwards set up Windows Hello and camera verification again. The recovery phrase keeps working.
help.windows.43: Settings › Unlocking › Master password › Change…. Enter the current one and the new one twice. To keep your recovery phrase working, also enter its 24 words; otherwise create a new phrase afterwards. Backups you already made keep the password they were made with.
help.windows.45: Lock button in the top bar, or Ctrl+L.
help.windows.46: Emergency lock: Ctrl+Alt+L anywhere in Windows. It locks at once and cancels any fill in progress.
help.windows.47: Lock after inactivity: Never, or 1 minute up to 24 hours.
help.windows.48: Lock when Windows locks (Win+L, switching user, signing out) and Lock on sleep (lid closed, sleep, hibernate).
help.windows.49: Never stay unlocked longer than: a hard limit, whatever you are doing.
help.windows.50: Count activity from: Computer activity or Vault activity.
help.windows.51: Ask before releasing 2FA codes to the browser extension.
help.windows.52: The tray icon menu has Open LocalGateKeys, Unlock vault, Lock vault, Lock & switch person, Quick access, Check for updates, switches for Browser integration and Desktop fill icons, and Exit.
help.windows.56: One entry per kind you have, such as Logins, Cards, Identities, Secure notes, Documents, Wi-Fi or Passkeys.
help.windows.60: Security center, Generator, Sync & devices, Devices & connections, Import & export, Trash. Settings is at the bottom.
help.windows.62: Search box, New item, Lock, and Ctrl K for the command palette.
help.windows.64: Cards for Password health, Backup & recovery, Coming up and Generator, plus One-time codes (click a code to copy it).
help.windows.67: Sort: Title A–Z, Title Z–A, Date modified, Date created.
help.windows.68: Flags on a row show a password that is Breached, Weak or Reused.
help.windows.69: Right-click a row (or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F10</kbd>) for Edit, Copy username, Copy password, Copy 2FA code, Open website, Share…, Add to favorites and Move to trash….
help.windows.71: Shows the fields of the selected item. Passwords stay hidden until you click them. Buttons copy the username, password or 2FA code, open the website, Edit, Share or Move to trash. Documents add Open file, Safe preview, Save a copy… and Replace file….
help.windows.73: Sign-ins: Website login, Desktop app login, Passkey
help.windows.74: Money: Payment card, Bank account · Personal: Identity, Secure note, Document
help.windows.75: Tech: SSH key, API key, Wi-Fi network, Bookmark · Things you own: License, Subscription, Warranty, Purchase
help.windows.76: Fill in the fields and choose Save. If you leave with unsaved changes you are asked Discard your changes?
help.windows.79: Change next to the password lets you type a new one, or choose Passphrase, Random or PIN to make one. Change it on the website too, then save.
help.windows.80: Two-factor: paste the site's setup key here (Pro). See Two-factor codes.
help.windows.81: Custom fields: Add field for anything else. Mark a field Hidden to treat it like a password.
help.windows.82: Password history: up to 5 old passwords are kept, encrypted, for a year. Copy previous password or Restore this password.
help.windows.83: Recovery codes: one per line. Copy and use next code copies one and removes it from the list.
help.windows.84: Autofill rules: Filling (On click or Off), Sign in after filling (Default, Never or Always), Always ask for the master password, and Offer to save changes from the browser.
help.windows.86: Each kind has its own fields. Dates are written as YYYY-MM-DD. Every item can be a Favorite and carry Tags (separate them with commas). Documents use Choose file and save (Pro).
help.windows.88: Collections group items your way: Add collection, Rename, Archive. They sync with your other devices, and you can share one with other people (see Shared collections).
help.windows.89: Reminders lists items that expire soon or are overdue, with Complete and Snooze 1 day.
help.windows.90: Activity shows a history of what happened in the vault.
help.windows.91: Select an item and choose Move to trash or press Delete.
help.windows.92: A message appears with Undo: click it to bring the item straight back.
help.windows.93: Later, open Tools › Trash and use Restore selected, Delete selected or Empty trash. Deleting from the trash cannot be undone.
help.windows.94: Settings › Privacy › Keep deleted items for sets 7, 14, 30 or 90 days, and Empty trash automatically clears it for you.

help.windows.96: Search: Ctrl+F, type, and press Enter to open the top result or ↓ to move into the list.

help.windows.100: Random: choose the length and which characters to use: A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and symbols.
help.windows.101: Passphrase: choose the number of words. Easier to type, just as strong when long enough.
help.windows.102: Generate again for a new one, Copy to copy it.

help.windows.119: Scan the QR code it shows (for several codes, scan each one: "Code 1 of 3 scanned").

help.windows.143: Bitwarden-compatible CSV, Bitwarden JSON, KeePass 2 XML: unencrypted. Delete them after use.

help.windows.158: Recovery phrase (Set up / Replace…) and Write recovery kit, a printable sheet.

help.iphone.16: Skip anything you like. A Finish setting up card at the top of the vault takes you back; Settings › Show setup again does too.

help.iphone.19: Settings › App password › turn on Use an app password.
help.iphone.20: Choose a strong password (at least 12 characters), and keep Unlock with Face ID on if you want it as a shortcut.
help.iphone.21: Write down the 24-word recovery phrase, tap I wrote them down, and type the three words it asks for.
help.iphone.23: Forgot it? Tap Forgot app password? on the unlock screen, type the 24 words, and choose a new app password.
help.iphone.24: If you add a new face or fingerprint to the iPhone, the Face ID shortcut turns off for safety: type the app password once and turn it back on.

help.iphone.28: Password history on a login keeps old passwords: copy or restore one (asks for Face ID).

help.iphone.30: Attach a file (Pro, up to 25 MB, stored encrypted) from +.

help.iphone.32: Sort by name or date, favourites first, or grouped by type.

help.iphone.52: Sign in to a site in Safari and tap Save in the prompt.

security.title: Security
security.description: How LocalGateKeys protects your vault and what it does not protect against.
security.the-security-model-in.1: The security model, in plain terms
security.the-security-model-in.2: What LocalGateKeys is designed to protect, and what it cannot protect.
security.how-your-vault-is.2: A random 256-bit key encrypts the vault. That key is never stored as it is; it is wrapped (encrypted) separately by each way you can unlock, so changing your password does not mean re-encrypting everything, and a wrapper copied from another vault is rejected.
security.how-your-vault-is.4: AES-256-GCM with a fresh random nonce for every save
security.how-your-vault-is.6: Argon2id, 3 passes, parallelism 4, random salt per wrapper; 256 MiB of memory in the Windows app (64 MiB on a PC with less than 4 GB of memory) and 64 MiB in the Mac, iPhone and Android apps
security.how-your-vault-is.8: Optional 24-word BIP39 phrase (256 bits), expanded with HKDF-SHA256
security.how-your-vault-is.9: Windows Hello, Touch ID, Face ID and fingerprint
security.how-your-vault-is.10: Release the vault key from storage the device protects; the master password is never stored
security.how-your-vault-is.12: Argon2id and AES-256-GCM with the parameters stored in the authenticated header
security.how-your-vault-is.14: A random group key, handed to each device with X25519 and HKDF-SHA256 and, for a cloud folder, also wrapped by your sync password with Argon2id; every record sealed with AES-256-GCM and bound to its item, version and key epoch; every device file bound to the device that wrote it
security.how-your-vault-is.16: ES256 (P-256) keys kept inside the encrypted vault; the app builds the signed data from the origin the browser reports, never from the page. The Microsoft Store app can also be the passkey provider of Windows 11 (off by default); Windows then keeps your passkey site and account names in its own list, never the keys
security.how-your-vault-is.18: Temporary file, flush, then atomic replace, so a crash cannot leave half a vault
security.designed-to-protect-against.2: Someone who copies your vault file or a backup and does not know your master password
security.designed-to-protect-against.3: A website getting logins or passkeys saved for a different website
security.designed-to-protect-against.4: Another program on your PC talking to LocalGateKeys without the session secret it hands to its own browser helper
security.designed-to-protect-against.5: Filling a desktop app that has been swapped, updated or changed since you bound it
security.designed-to-protect-against.8: Your cloud provider reading synced data: it only stores ciphertext
security.not-able-to-protect.2: Malware, or anyone with administrator control, already running on your PC
security.not-able-to-protect.3: A compromised browser, Windows installation or dependency
security.not-able-to-protect.4: A website you deliberately fill a password into
security.not-able-to-protect.5: Someone using your PC while the vault is unlocked
security.not-able-to-protect.6: Phishing inside a genuine app that shows attacker-controlled content
security.not-able-to-protect.7: Losing your vault, your backups and your master password with no recovery phrase: nobody, including us, can open it
security.things-localgatekeys-never-does: Some ways of filling passwords are indistinguishable from spyware, so they are ruled out by design. LocalGateKeys contains no:
screen reading or OCR to find credentials
decryption of your browser's saved-password database
code injection into other programs or games
submitting a sign-in you did not start
security.the-network-honestly.2: There is no LocalGateKeys account and no server that holds vaults. The app connects to the internet in only these cases:
security.the-network-honestly.3: Updates. The Microsoft Store updates the Windows app and the App Store updates the Mac and iPhone apps; LocalGateKeys itself never downloads or runs an installer. The retired Windows installer builds (up to 0.4.12, the last one) download one small file from our server when you choose Check for updates and verify its signature with a key built into the app.
security.the-network-honestly.4: Licence revocation list. With each update check in the installer builds, and when you choose Check for updates in the Microsoft Store app with strict offline mode off, the app downloads a signed list of refunded licences and checks your licence against it on your PC. It sends nothing about your licence.
security.the-network-honestly.5: Website icons. To show a site's icon, the app downloads it from that site's own address. No username, password or vault data is sent, but each download tells that site, and anyone watching the network, that your vault has an account there. This is off by default and only happens if you turn on "Show website icons" in Settings; strict offline mode blocks it.
security.the-network-honestly.6: Breach checks, if you turn them on. When you start a check, the app sends the first five characters of each password's SHA-1 hash to Have I Been Pwned. The service sees your IP address, never the password, the full hash, the username or the website.
security.the-network-honestly.7: Sync, if you set it up. Over your home network, devices talk to each other directly. Through a cloud folder, your cloud-drive app does the uploading.
security.the-network-honestly.8: Strict offline mode is on by default. It blocks background internet requests, website icons and breach checks, and an update check asks you first. The privacy policy lists exactly what our servers see when you do check for updates.
security.known-limitations.2: The master password is moved into a wipeable buffer as soon as it reaches the app and is erased when the operation that needed it finishes. The page you type it into runs in Microsoft Edge WebView2. The page empties its field and the app lets go of the copy made by the hand-off before your key is computed, but neither of those two copies can be overwritten in memory, so traces can remain there for a short time.
security.known-limitations.3: Camera unlock asks for a random head movement, so a photo held flat in front of the camera, or a still picture on a screen, does not pass. It is still a convenience check, not certified protection: a bent or folded photo, a video that follows the prompts, or a mask may pass. Windows Hello is the stronger choice.
security.known-limitations.4: Windows app fill does not work with programs running as administrator, custom-drawn game interfaces, or embedded web views it cannot verify.
security.known-limitations.5: The vault detects being rolled back to an older copy. If you use sync, your other devices remember how new your vault was, so an older copy put back on one device is reported at the next sync, in every app. Without sync, a Windows PC keeps a second record outside the vault folder, so an older vault put back together with its anchor file is refused; someone who can change your Windows account's settings can remove that record too. The iPhone, Mac and Android apps keep their files closed to other apps, but without sync they do not notice an older copy put back in their place.
security.known-limitations.6: Passkeys work in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Signing in with a passkey inside another site's frame works in Chrome and Edge when the surrounding site allows it; in Firefox, and when you create a passkey inside another site's frame, the browser's own passkey dialog is used. If a site cancels after you approve a new passkey, the app removes it again; when the app cannot tell whether the site kept it, the passkey stays in your vault and you can delete it in the app.
security.report-a-vulnerability.2: Email {{SECURITY_EMAIL}}. The vulnerability disclosure policy explains what is in scope, how quickly we respond and how we credit researchers.
security.source.title: Source code for security audits
security.source.body: LocalGateKeys is source-available: the full source code is published on GitHub so anyone can check how it protects your vault. The licence (PolyForm Strict, with a security research permission) lets you read, build and test the code privately to find and report vulnerabilities. It is not open source: copying, redistributing or selling it is not allowed.
support.title: Support and FAQ
support.description: Answers to common questions about LocalGateKeys on Windows, Mac and iPhone: master passwords, Pro licences, sync, sharing and refunds, and how to contact support.
support.support-and-questions.2: Most answers are below. For anything else, email {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}. Never send us your master password, recovery phrase or vault file; we will never ask for them.
support.your-vault.2: I forgot my master password. Can you reset it?
support.your-vault.3: No. We never have your master password or your vault, so there is nothing we could reset. If you created a recovery phrase, use it on the unlock screen to open the vault and set a new password.
support.your-vault.4: Without the password or the recovery phrase, the vault cannot be opened by anyone. Backups are encrypted with their own backup password, so a backup you can still open is the other way back in.
support.your-vault.5: Do you keep a copy of my vault?
support.your-vault.6: No. There is no LocalGateKeys account or server that stores vaults. Your vault exists only on your devices and in any backups or cloud folders you set up yourself.
support.your-vault.7: Where is the vault stored on my PC?
support.your-vault.8: In your Windows user profile, under %LOCALAPPDATA%\LocalGateKeys. Copying that file somewhere else is safe, because it is encrypted, but use scheduled backups rather than copying the live file.
support.your-vault.9: Can I import from another password manager?
support.your-vault.10: Yes. Choose Import & export in the app and pick the export file from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass or KeePassXC (a .kdbx file opens directly), Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox or Safari. Any other CSV file works too: you tell the app which column is which. You review every item before anything is written, and the import never goes online. Afterwards, delete the export file, because most exports hold your passwords in plain text.
support.your-vault.11: Does it work without an internet connection?
support.your-vault.12: Yes, completely. The app uses the network only for update checks (which also fetch the licence revocation list), breach checks you start, website icons if you turn them on, and sync if you set it up. Strict offline mode, on by default, blocks background requests, website icons and breach checks and asks before an update check. See the security page.
support.filling-sign-ins.2: Why does the browser extension need the desktop app?
support.filling-sign-ins.3: The vault is kept in the desktop app, not in the browser. The extension asks the app, through a small local helper, for the logins that match the site you are on. That way the browser never holds your whole vault. Install the app first, then add the extension from the download page.
support.filling-sign-ins.5: Yes. In Chrome and Edge on Windows, when a website offers a passkey, the extension asks whether to save it in LocalGateKeys, and you approve it in the desktop app. Signing in with it works the same way. You can always choose the browser's own passkey dialog instead, or turn passkeys off in the app's autofill settings. On iPhone, you can choose LocalGateKeys for passkeys in AutoFill. Passkeys count as items toward the free plan's 7-item limit.
support.filling-sign-ins.6: A Windows app will not fill. Why?
support.filling-sign-ins.7: Windows app fill only works when the app exposes real sign-in fields to Windows. It will refuse when:
support.filling-sign-ins.8: the app has been updated since you bound it, so its fingerprint changed; bind it again
support.filling-sign-ins.9: the app runs as administrator and LocalGateKeys does not
support.filling-sign-ins.10: the sign-in screen is drawn by a game engine or an embedded web page that cannot be verified
support.filling-sign-ins.11: These refusals are deliberate. LocalGateKeys will not fall back to recording or simulating keystrokes blindly.
support.filling-sign-ins.13: No. It installs no keyboard hook and never watches what you type. See things LocalGateKeys never does.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.3: Unlimited items, device sync, two-factor codes (also on Apple Watch) and documents. The free edition holds up to 7 items: logins, notes, cards, identities and every other kind count, items in the trash do not. See pricing.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.4: What happens if I have more than 7 items without Pro?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.5: Nothing is taken away. This can happen after upgrading from an older version or after removing a licence. Every item stays usable, editable and fillable; you just cannot add a new one until you buy Pro or go back under 7.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.6: Do I have to pay again for updates?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.7: No. Pro is a single payment that includes every future update. There is no subscription and nothing to renew.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.8: How many PCs can I use Pro on?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.9: All the PCs you personally use. The licence is for one person; please buy one for each member of your household or team.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.10: How do I turn on Pro, and what if I lose my key?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.11: After payment you see your licence key straight away, with a file to download. Choose Install in LocalGateKeys on that page, or paste the key in Tools > Licence. The key is also saved inside your encrypted vault, so restoring a backup restores Pro. See your Pro licence.
support.v2.iphone-pro.q: I bought Pro on my iPhone. Does my PC get it too?
support.v2.iphone-pro.a: Yes. Pair the PC with your iPhone, and a free PC takes the licence over sync and becomes Pro. Or choose Copy key in the iPhone's Settings and install the key on the PC in Tools > Licence. The iPhone app sends only the App Store receipt to our licence server.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.13: Yes, a full refund within 30 days of purchase, no questions asked. A refunded licence is revoked, so the 7-item limit applies again; every existing item stays usable. See the refund policy.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.14: Who handles the payment, and can I get an invoice?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.15: {{MERCHANT_OF_RECORD}} sells Pro on our behalf as merchant of record. They take the payment, apply the right VAT or sales tax and issue receipts and invoices, including invoices with your company's VAT number.
support.sync-and-iphone.2: Does Wi-Fi sync go over the internet?
support.sync-and-iphone.3: No. Paired devices on the same network connect to each other directly, over a connection that is authenticated and encrypted. Both need to be unlocked. Sync is part of Pro.
support.sync-and-iphone.4: What can my cloud provider see if I sync through a cloud folder?
support.sync-and-iphone.5: Encrypted files, how many there are, their sizes and when they change, and a list of your devices' random IDs and public keys. Not the names, usernames, passwords or anything else inside your vault. Your provider's own terms apply to the files you store with them.
support.sync-and-iphone.7: Yes. Get LocalGateKeys on the App Store. It syncs with your Windows PC and Mac, shows the two-factor codes you choose on your Apple Watch and, like the Windows app, collects no data.An iPhone app is coming. It will sync with your Windows PC and, like the Windows app, will collect no data.
support.v2.share.q: How do I share one login with someone?
support.v2.share.a: Select the item and choose Share. LocalGateKeys makes a .lgkshare file or a QR code, locked with a six-word code. Send the file, then tell the person the six words another way, such as by phone. It opens once, and three wrong codes destroy it. See the user guide.
support.v2.mac-android.q: Is there a Mac or Android app?
support.v2.mac-android.a: The Mac app is on the Mac App Store. The Android app is coming; it is not on Google Play yet. Until then, the Windows, Mac and iPhone apps sync with each other.

switch.caveat: Passkeys do not transfer in a CSV export; LocalGateKeys imports them from CXF files (Apple Passwords and other apps that export CXF) on PC, Android, iPhone and Mac.
switch.checked: Facts on this page were checked on 8 November 2026; each one links to its source.
switch.import.csv: In LocalGateKeys, choose Import, pick the CSV file and check the preview. LocalGateKeys recognises the format and maps the columns; nothing is saved until you confirm. Then delete the CSV file, because it holds your passwords unencrypted.
switch.import.cxf: On Mac or iPhone, start the transfer from Apple Passwords and choose LocalGateKeys. On PC and Android, import the CSV file instead: choose Import, pick the file, check the preview and confirm. Delete any CSV file afterwards, because it holds your passwords unencrypted.
switch.import.1pux: In LocalGateKeys, choose Import and pick the .1pux file (or the CSV file). Check the preview and confirm, then delete the export file, because it holds your passwords unencrypted.
switch.import.kdbx: In LocalGateKeys, choose Import, pick your .kdbx database and enter its master password. Your KeePass file is only read, never changed.
switch.import.json: In LocalGateKeys, choose Import and pick the .json file. Check the preview and confirm, then delete the export file, because it holds your passwords unencrypted.
switch.loss.passkeys: Passkeys, unless they move in a CXF transfer (see the note above).
switch.loss.shared: Items in shared vaults or collections you do not own. Export them while you still have access, or ask the owner to.
switch.loss.attachments: File attachments. Save them separately before you close your old account.
switch.loss.attachments_csv: File attachments, because a CSV file holds text only. Save them separately before you close your old account.
switch.loss.only_passwords: Anything beyond logins: the export holds the website, username, password and sometimes a note.
switch.price: LocalGateKeys Pro is {{PRICE}} once. One payment. Every update, forever, free. The free version holds up to 7 items, with no time limit.
switch.1password.export.1: In the 1Password desktop app, choose File → Export and pick your account.
switch.1password.export.2: Choose the 1PUX format (it keeps more item types) or CSV, enter your account password and save the file.
switch.1password.why.1: March 2026: 1Password raised its Individual and Families prices, as comparison sites reported.
switch.bitwarden.export.1: In the Bitwarden web vault or desktop app, open Tools → Export vault.
switch.bitwarden.export.2: Choose .json (unencrypted), confirm with your master password and save the file. A password-protected .json export also works.
switch.bitwarden.why.1: February 2026: Bitwarden changed its Premium plan, with a reported price increase (sources differ on the amount).
switch.lastpass.export.1: In LastPass, open Advanced → Export and choose a CSV file.
switch.lastpass.export.2: Enter your master password and save the CSV file.
switch.dashlane.export.1: In Dashlane, choose Export and pick CSV. Dashlane saves a .zip of CSV files; keep it as it is.
switch.dashlane.export.2: Enter your master password if asked and save the file.
switch.dashlane.why.1: September 2025: Dashlane removed its free plan.
switch.enpass.export.1: In Enpass, choose File → Export, pick the vault and choose CSV.
switch.enpass.export.2: Enter your master password and save the file. In LocalGateKeys, match the columns once in the import preview.
switch.enpass.why.1: 14 September 2026: Enpass renamed its free tier Enpass Free, limited to 25 items and one vault on desktop.
switch.keepass.export.1: There is nothing to export: LocalGateKeys reads your KeePass .kdbx database directly.
switch.keepass.export.2: Keep a copy of the .kdbx file if you like. KeePassXC and other KeePass apps use the same file.
switch.proton-pass.export.1: In Proton Pass, open Settings → Export.
switch.proton-pass.export.2: Choose CSV, or the unencrypted Proton Pass .zip export, confirm and save the file.
switch.proton-pass.why.1: January 2026: Proton Pass added biometric unlock for Plus plans and above, not for the free plan.
switch.nordpass.export.1: In the NordPass desktop app, open Settings → Export items.
switch.nordpass.export.2: Confirm with your master password and save the CSV file.
switch.apple-passwords.export.1: On macOS 26, open Passwords, choose File → Export to App and pick LocalGateKeys. This moves passkeys too.
switch.apple-passwords.export.2: Or choose File → Export → CSV to save a CSV file for any LocalGateKeys app (passwords only).
switch.google.export.1: Go to passwords.google.com, open Settings and choose Export passwords.
switch.google.export.2: Confirm with your Google account and save the CSV file.
switch.microsoft-authenticator.export.1: In Microsoft Authenticator, open Settings → Export passwords, if the app still holds your passwords.
switch.microsoft-authenticator.export.2: In Microsoft Edge, open Settings → Passwords → Export passwords and save the CSV file.
switch.microsoft-authenticator.why.1: June to August 2025: Microsoft Authenticator stopped storing and autofilling passwords; Microsoft points users to Edge.

security.the-network-honestly.10: Verified site. The lookalike check runs on your device. Your saved sites never leave the app, and nothing is sent to a server.
security.known-limitations.7: The lookalike warning is a hint, not a wall: a page's own script can bypass it, for example by sending a password without a form submit. Check the address yourself.

features.v3.emergency.title: Emergency access and duress password (Pro)
features.v3.emergency.2: Split your recovery phrase into up to five shards for people you trust. Any chosen number of them (two to five) can get back in. Each person gets a signed file, a QR code or a printed sheet. There is no account and no server: you share a folder, such as a cloud folder or a USB stick, with them.
features.v3.emergency.4: A person who needs access asks from their own LocalGateKeys. After the waiting period you chose (1 to 30 days) the app opens a copy of your latest encrypted backup. Until then, any of your devices can say No. You can also grant access at once. Phones end the flow by showing your recovery phrase; open the backup on a computer.
features.v3.emergency.6: Nothing outside the apps enforces the waiting period or your No. Any group of holders that holds enough shards, working together, can open your backup at once. Choose people who would not act together and keep the shards apart. Replacing your recovery phrase makes old shards useless.
features.v3.emergency.8: A second password opens a believable vault with sample items and shows nothing about your real one. While it is open, the real vault stays locked for the hours you choose, and nothing syncs. It hides your vault from someone looking over your shoulder or forcing you to open the app. It does not hide that the feature exists from someone who examines your files. On Windows, Mac, iPhone and Android.
security.v3.limit.emergency: Emergency access has no server, so only the apps enforce the waiting period and your veto. Anyone who holds enough shards can recover your backup at once, without waiting. Pick holders who would not act together, and keep the shards apart.
security.v3.limit.duress: The duress password defends against being forced to unlock the app. It does not defend against someone who examines the files on your disk, and a careful person can find out that a second vault exists. It is on Windows, the Mac, iPhone and Android.
security.v4.spec.agents.2: Off by default (Pro). An agent reaches the app only through lgk mcp on your own device and sees only the logins and items you allowed. You approve each request; the app fills the sign-in itself, and no reply to the agent contains a password. Each request goes into an access log whose entries are chained with SHA-256 hashes, and the Security check says whether that chain is intact
security.v4.protect.panel: A web page reading the accounts LocalGateKeys offers you: in Chrome, Edge and Firefox the list is drawn in a separate extension frame the page cannot read
security.v4.protect.agents: An AI agent getting a password from LocalGateKeys: no reply to the agent contains one, and it sees only the logins you allowed
security.v4.limit.agents: An AI agent that controls your browser reading a password after LocalGateKeys has filled it into the page, or a command you approved passing on the secrets it was given
security.v4.network.licence: Buying Pro in the Mac, iPhone or Android app. The app sends the store's signed purchase record to our licence server, which answers with your licence key. No email address and no device data are sent.
security.v4.network.ledger: In the Windows app, Security center › Network activity lists each of these connections with the time, the host and the result. The names of websites you saved are shown only while the app runs and are never written to disk, and devices on your own network appear as "Local network".
features.v3.power.title: Power-user tools
features.v3.power.2: Once a week, LocalGateKeys restores your newest backup into a scratch folder, checks that it opens, and deletes the copy. It tells you if the backup uses an old password.
features.v3.power.4: Opens the page where you change a site's password: from a curated list, the standard /.well-known/change-password address, or the sign-in page. It never fills in third-party sites.
features.v3.power.6: Keep separate vaults, such as Work and Personal. The free plan holds one vault. The 7-item free limit counts across all vaults.
features.v3.power.8: A one-page report you can print. It contains no passwords and no item names.
features.v3.power.10: Shares can expire after 1 hour or 1 day, work only once, and be revoked. This is best effort.
features.v3.power.12: A template for executors, next to emergency access.
features.v3.dev.title: For developers and AI agents
features.v3.dev.1: AI agents sign in, your passwords stay on your PC (Pro)
features.v3.dev.2: Claude Code and other MCP agents can ask LocalGateKeys to sign in to a site. You approve each request, the browser extension fills the form, and the agent never sees the password. On Windows: claude mcp add localgatekeys -- LocalGateKeysNativeHost.exe mcp (the Microsoft Store app also runs the lgk command line as LocalGateKeysNativeHost.exe lgk).
features.v3.dev.4: Each activity entry is linked to the one before it by a hash, so the Security check shows when the log was changed, cut short or emptied.
news.agents.title: AI agents can sign in, your passwords stay on your PC
news.agents.description: LocalGateKeys Pro lets AI agents such as Claude Code sign in to a site you approve, without ever seeing the password.
news.agents.1: AI agents can sign in, your passwords stay on your PC
news.agents.2: AI agents can now do work in your browser that needs a sign-in, without getting your password. The agent asks to sign in to one site, you approve it in LocalGateKeys, and the browser extension fills the sign-in form. The agent learns only whether the form was filled.
news.agents.3: Each approval works once, for five minutes, on that site only. Logins that ask for your master password every time are never used. An agent can ask only a few times a minute, and every request goes into an access log that shows if it was changed.
news.agents.4: It is off by default and needs Pro. Turn it on in Settings › Developer. It runs on Windows through the lgk command line tool; in the Microsoft Store version it runs as LocalGateKeysNativeHost.exe lgk.

help.v3.win.safety.1: Emergency access (Pro): on the Backup & restore page choose Set up emergency access. Your recovery phrase is split into shards for people you trust; you choose how many shards are needed and a waiting period. Give each holder their sheet or shard file.
help.v3.win.safety.2: When enough holders ask for access through the shared folder, your devices show the request and you can Deny it until the waiting period ends. help.v3.win.safety.3: Estate pack, on the same page, creates a note for your heirs (where the will is, accounts to close, devices and who holds a shard), then the Emergency kit to print.
help.v3.win.safety.4: Duress password (Pro): Settings › Unlocking › Duress password › Set up. It is a second master password for when someone forces you to unlock. help.v3.win.shared.1: Share one collection with family or a team through a folder you all can reach, such as a shared OneDrive folder. Open the collection, choose Share collection, pick the folder, choose whether members can edit or only view, and set a share password.
help.v3.win.shared.2: The others choose Join a shared collection, pick the folder and type the share password; you then choose Let them in. Only that collection goes through the folder: your other items stay private. You can remove a person, Stop sharing or leave at any time.
